def: A network that reads a sequence one step at a time, applying the same cell at every step and carrying a hidden state forward.
The fixed-size vector a recurrent network carries from step to step as a summary of everything read so far.
Training a recurrent network by unrolling it over the sequence and backpropagating through every step, summing gradients for the shared weights.
Backpropagation through time over chunks of a long sequence, passing the state between chunks but stopping gradients at their boundaries.
The shrinking of gradients towards zero as they are multiplied through many steps, so early inputs get almost no learning signal.
The growth of gradients without bound as they are multiplied through many steps, causing huge updates or NaN values.
Rescaling the whole gradient to a maximum norm when it grows too large, limiting step size without changing direction.
A recurrent cell with a separate cell state updated additively under learned forget, input and output gates, which lets gradients survive over longer spans.
The LSTM's long-term memory vector, updated by scaling the old value with the forget gate and adding gated new content.
A learned vector of numbers between 0 and 1, produced by a sigmoid, that scales how much of another vector passes through.
A gated recurrent unit that merges the LSTM's cell and hidden state and uses two gates, with similar behaviour at lower cost.
A design in which one network reads the source sequence into a summary and another generates the target sequence from it.
Letting a model, at each output step, take a weighted sum over all states of the input, with weights computed from the current need.
